name.text: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — exact values and the principal range

questiontext.text:
Find the exact value of \( {@invname@}({@val@}) \), giving your answer in radians (a multiple of \(\pi\)).

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The inverse trig functions are defined with a restricted (principal) range so that they give exactly one answer:

  • \(\sin^{-1}\) always returns a value in \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\)
  • \(\cos^{-1}\) always returns a value in \([0,\pi]\)
  • \(\tan^{-1}\) always returns a value in \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\)

Even though other angles also satisfy the underlying trig equation, only the one inside the principal range is the correct value of the inverse function. Here \( {@invname@}({@val@}) = {@ta@} \).
